newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Warm, dry weather holds in Brazil CS sugar areas.
newsitem.headline: Warm, dry weather holds in Brazil CS sugar areas.

text.p: Warm, dry weather is continuing practically throughout the sugar cane growing region in Brazil's center-south, independent consultants DataNet-AgriCommodities said in a regular weather update.
High maximum temperatures are being seen in the states of Sao Paulo and Parana, which DataNet attributes to the El Nino weather phenomenon developing in the Pacific Ocean.
The absence of rains in the four weeks has brought crushings of the 1997/98 sugar harvest back to normal, particularly since the beginning of July.

In Sao Paulo state which accounts for 74 percent of sugar cane output in the region, crushings in the second half of June were still hit by impurities in the cane caused by the marshy ground, DataNet said.
Humidity levels combined with the temperatures meant that sugar content this month should stay the same as last month without the hoped-for seasonal growth, it added.
On Thursday the Sao Paulo sugar association Unica released figures for center-south production up to July 1.
The figures showed a 0.67 percent fall in sugar cane output campared with the same stage last year and a 1.99 percent drop in sugar production.
Alcohol production however was running 6.59 percent up on last year to July 1.
